units.zh: 李勉，字玄卿，鄭王元懿曾孫也。
units.en: Li Mian, whose courtesy name was Xuanqing, was a great-grandson of Prince Zheng, Yuanyi.
units.literal: Li Mian, styled Xuanqing, was a great-grandson of Prince Zheng Yuanyi.

units.zh: 父擇言，為漢褒相岐四州刺史、安德郡公，所歷皆以嚴干聞。
units.en: His father Zeyan held the posts of prefect over Han, Bao, Xiang, and Qi and bore the title Duke of Ande; wherever he served, he was known for stern efficiency.
units.literal: His father Zeyan served as prefect of the four prefectures Han, Bao, Xiang, and Qi, and as Duke of Ande; in every post he was known for severity and capability.

units.zh: 在漢州，張嘉貞為益州長史、判都督事，性簡貴，待管內刺史禮隔，而引擇言同榻，坐談政理，時人榮之。
units.en: When Zeyan was in Han Prefecture, Zhang Jiazhen served as chief secretary of Yizhou and acted as military governor. Aloof and proud by nature, Zhang kept the prefects in his circuit at a formal distance, yet invited Zeyan to share his couch and discuss affairs of government; contemporaries regarded this as a signal honor.
units.literal: While in Han Prefecture, Zhang Jiazhen was chief secretary of Yizhou and handled the military governorship; by nature aloof and eminent, he kept distant ceremonial distance from the prefects under his jurisdiction, yet drew Zeyan to share his couch and sit discussing governance; men of the time took this as an honor.

units.zh: 勉幼勤經史，長而沉雅清峻，宗於虛玄，以近屬陪位，累授開封尉。
units.en: As a boy Mian applied himself diligently to the classics and histories. In maturity he was reserved, refined, and austere, inclined toward Daoist subtlety, and through proximity to the throne was repeatedly appointed marshal of Kaifeng.
units.literal: Mian in youth applied himself to the classics and histories; grown up, he was grave, elegant, clear, and lofty, devoted to the abstruse and mystical, and by virtue of close imperial kinship received successive appointments as marshal of Kaifeng.

units.zh: 時升平日久，且汴州水陸所湊，邑居龐雜，號為難理，勉與聯尉盧成軌等，並有擒奸擿伏之名。
units.en: Peace had lasted many years, and Bianzhou—where land and water traffic met—was crowded and chaotic, notorious as difficult to administer. Mian, along with associate marshal Lu Chenggui and others, earned a reputation for apprehending wrongdoers and uncovering concealed crimes.
units.literal: The age was long at peace, and moreover Bianzhou, where land and water routes converged, had sprawling, tangled settlements and was called hard to govern; Mian, together with the associate marshal Lu Chenggui and others, all won fame for seizing villains and exposing hidden crimes.

units.zh: 至德初，從至靈武，拜監察御史。
units.en: In the early Zhide period he accompanied the court to Lingwu and was appointed investigating censor.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Zhide era he followed the emperor to Lingwu and was appointed investigating censor.

units.zh: 屬朝廷右武，勳臣恃寵，多不知禮。
units.en: The court at the time favored military power, and meritorious officials, trusting in imperial favor, often showed little regard for propriety.
units.literal: It happened that the court favored military men; meritorious ministers, relying on favor, for the most part did not know ritual propriety.

units.zh: 大將管崇嗣於行在朝堂背闕而坐，言笑自若，勉劾之，拘於有司，肅宗特原之，歎曰：「吾有李勉，始知朝廷尊也。」
units.en: The general Guan Congsi sat in the mobile court's audience hall with his back to the throne, chatting and laughing as though unconcerned. Mian impeached him and had him held by the proper authorities. Emperor Suzong personally pardoned Guan and sighed, "Only with Li Mian do I learn that the court commands respect."
units.literal: The great general Guan Congsi at the mobile court sat in the audience hall with his back to the imperial presence, talking and laughing as if at ease; Mian impeached him and had him detained by the appropriate office; Suzong specially pardoned him and sighed, saying, "With Li Mian, I now know that the court is honored."

units.zh: 遷司膳員外郎。
units.en: He was promoted to vice director in the Office of Provisions.
units.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Office of Provisions.

units.zh: 時關東獻俘百餘，詔並處斬，囚有仰天歎者，勉過問之，對曰：「某被脅制守官，非逆者。」
units.en: More than a hundred captives from east of the Pass were presented at court, and an edict ordered them all put to death. One prisoner looked up to heaven and sighed. Mian stopped to question him, and the man answered, "I was forced to hold office under duress; I was no rebel."
units.literal: At the time more than a hundred captives from east of the Pass were presented; an edict ordered them all executed. Among the prisoners one sighed toward heaven; Mian passed by and questioned him, and he replied, "I was coerced into holding office and was not a rebel."

units.zh: 勉乃哀之，上言曰：「元惡未殄，遭點污者半天下，皆欲澡心歸化。
units.en: Moved to pity, Mian memorialized the throne: "The chief villain is not yet destroyed. Half the empire has been tainted by association, and all wish to purify their hearts and submit. If we execute them all, we will drive the world into the rebels' arms.
units.literal: Mian then pitied him and memorialized, saying, "The chief villain is not yet destroyed; those who were stained number half the empire, and all wish to cleanse their hearts and return to allegiance.

units.zh: 若盡殺之，是驅天下以資兇逆也。」
units.en: To slaughter them all would be to drive the whole world to feed the rebels."
units.literal: If we kill them all, this is driving the empire to supply the vicious and rebellious."

units.zh: 肅宗遽令奔騎宥釋，由是歸化日至。
units.en: Suzong at once sent mounted couriers to pardon and release them, and thereafter submissions came in day by day.
units.literal: Suzong immediately ordered mounted couriers to pardon and release them; from this day submissions increased daily.

units.zh: 克復西京，累歷清要，四遷至河南少尹。
units.en: After the recovery of Chang'an he rose through a series of prestigious posts, reaching vice governor of Henan after four promotions.
units.literal: After recovering the Western Capital, he passed through successive posts of pure and important rank, being promoted four times to vice governor of Henan.

units.zh: 累為河東節度王思禮、朔方河東都統李國貞行軍司馬，尋遷梁州都督、山南西道觀察使。
units.en: He served successively as expeditionary vice marshal under Hedong military governor Wang Sil and under Shuofang-Hedong supreme commander Li Guozhen, then was appointed military governor of Liangzhou and observation commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
units.literal: He repeatedly served as expeditionary vice marshal for Hedong military governor Wang Sil and for Shuofang-Hedong supreme commander Li Guozhen, and soon was transferred to military governor of Liangzhou and observation commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.

units.zh: 勉以故吏前密縣尉王晬勤干，俾攝南鄭令，俄有詔處死，勉問其故，乃為權幸所誣。
units.en: Mian had appointed his former subordinate Wang Hui, once magistrate of Mi County, to act as magistrate of Nanzheng on account of his diligence and ability. Soon an edict ordered Wang's execution. When Mian inquired, he learned that Wang had been framed by powerful favorites at court.
units.literal: Mian, because his former subordinate Wang Hui, former magistrate of Mi County, was diligent and capable, had him act as magistrate of Nanzheng; shortly an edict ordered his execution; Mian inquired the reason and found he had been slandered by the powerful and favored.

units.zh: 勉詢將吏曰：「上方藉牧宰為人父母，豈以譖言而殺不辜乎！」
units.en: Mian asked his officers and staff, "The throne now depends on local magistrates to be fathers and mothers to the people. How can it put an innocent man to death on a whispered accusation?"
units.literal: Mian questioned his generals and officials, saying, "His Majesty now relies on local administrators as fathers and mothers to the people—how can he kill the innocent on the basis of slander!"

units.zh: 即停詔拘晬，飛表上聞，晬遂獲宥，而勉竟為執政所非，追入為大理少卿。
units.en: He at once withheld the edict, detained Wang Hui, and sent an urgent memorial to the throne. Wang was spared, but Mian was censured by the chief ministers and recalled to the capital as vice minister of justice.
units.literal: He immediately halted the edict, detained Hui, and sent an urgent memorial to inform the throne; Hui thus obtained pardon, but Mian in the end was faulted by those in power and was recalled to serve as vice minister of justice.

units.zh: 謁見，面陳王晬無罪，政事條舉，盡力吏也。
units.en: On presenting himself at court he told the emperor face to face that Wang Hui was innocent, that his administration was thorough and well ordered, and that he was an official who gave his utmost.
units.literal: On audience he stated to the emperor's face that Wang Hui was guiltless, that his administration was orderly in every respect, and that he was an official who gave his full effort.

units.zh: 肅宗嘉其守正，乃除太常少卿。
units.en: Suzong commended his integrity and appointed him vice minister of rites.
units.literal: Suzong praised his uprightness and appointed him vice minister of rites.

units.zh: 王晬後以推擇拜大理評事、龍門令，終有能名，時稱知人。
units.en: Wang Hui was later recommended and appointed reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Longmen. He retained a reputation for competence to the end, and contemporaries praised Mian for discerning talent.
units.literal: Wang Hui later, through recommendation, was appointed reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Longmen; to the end he had a reputation for ability, and men of the time praised Mian for knowing men.

units.zh: 肅宗將大用勉，會李輔國寵任，意欲勉降禮於己。
units.en: Suzong was on the point of giving Mian major responsibility when Li Fuguo, then in high favor, expected Mian to show him deference.
units.literal: Suzong was about to employ Mian on a grand scale when Li Fuguo, enjoying favor and trust, wished Mian to lower ritual deference toward himself.

units.zh: 勉不為之屈，竟為所抑，出歷汾州、虢州刺史，改京兆尹、檢校右庶子、兼御史中丞、都畿觀察使。
units.en: Mian refused to bend and was ultimately blocked by Li Fuguo. He was sent out as prefect of Fen and Guo, then appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, acting right vice grand mentor, censor-in-chief, and observation commissioner of the capital region.
units.literal: Mian would not yield to him and in the end was suppressed by him; he went out to serve successively as prefect of Fenzhou and Guozhou, then was changed to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, made acting right vice grand mentor, and concurrently censor-in-chief and observation commissioner of the capital region.

units.zh: 尋兼河南尹，明年罷尹，以中丞歸西台，又除江西觀察使。
units.en: He soon also served as metropolitan governor of Henan. The following year he left that post and returned to the Censorate as chief censor, then was appointed observation commissioner of Jiangxi.
units.literal: Soon he was additionally made metropolitan governor of Henan; the next year he was removed as governor and returned to the western bureau as censor-in-chief, then was appointed observation commissioner of Jiangxi.

units.zh: 賊帥陳莊連陷江西州縣，偏將呂太一、武日升相繼背叛，勉與諸道力戰，悉攻平之。
units.en: The rebel leader Chen Zhuang overran prefectures and counties across Jiangxi. Subordinate generals Lü Taiyi and Wu Risheng rebelled in succession. Mian fought alongside troops from other circuits and subdued them all.
units.literal: The bandit chief Chen Zhuang successively seized prefectures and counties of Jiangxi; the subordinate generals Lü Taiyi and Wu Risheng rebelled in turn; Mian fought hard together with the various circuits and attacked and pacified them all.

units.zh: 部人有父病，以蠱道為木偶人，署勉名位，瘞於其隴，或以告，曰：「為父禳災，亦可矜也。」
units.en: A subordinate whose father was ill used sorcery to fashion a wooden figure, inscribed it with Mian's name and title, and buried it on his father's grave. When someone reported this, Mian said, "He did it to ward off disaster for his father. That deserves pity."
units.literal: A man of his command, whose father was ill, used sorcery to make a wooden doll, inscribed it with Mian's name and rank, and buried it on his father's mound; someone reported this, and Mian said, "He did it to avert disaster for his father—this may be pitied."

units.zh: 捨之。
units.en: He released the man without punishment.
units.literal: He let the matter go.

units.zh: 大歷二年，來朝，拜京兆尹、兼御史大夫，政尚簡肅。
units.en: In 767 he came to court and was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and censor grandee. His rule was marked by simplicity and austerity.
units.literal: In the second year of the Dali era he came to court and was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and concurrently censor grandee; his administration favored simplicity and severity.

units.zh: 宦官魚朝恩為觀軍容使，仍知國子監事，恃寵含威，天憲在舌。
units.en: The eunuch Yu Chao'en served as army-observing commissioner and also supervised the Imperial University. Trusting in imperial favor, he wielded intimidating power as though the law itself were his to pronounce.
units.literal: The eunuch Yu Chao'en was army-observing commissioner and still supervised the Directorate of Education; relying on favor he harbored authority, and the laws of heaven rested on his tongue.

units.zh: 前尹黎干寫心候事，動必求媚，每朝恩入監，傾府人吏具數百人之餼以待之。
units.en: The previous governor, Li Gan, fawned on him in every matter. Whenever Yu Chao'en visited the directorate, Li mobilized the entire prefectural staff to prepare food for hundreds of men.
units.literal: The previous governor Li Gan laid bare his heart in waiting on affairs and in every move sought to flatter; whenever Chao'en entered the directorate, he emptied the prefectural staff to prepare provisions for several hundred men to await him.

units.zh: 及勉蒞職旬月，朝恩入監，府吏先期有請，勉曰：「軍容使判國子監事，勉候太學，軍容宜厚具主禮。
units.en: About ten days after Mian took office, Yu Chao'en came to the directorate. The prefectural clerks asked in advance how to receive him. Mian said, "As army-observing commissioner supervising the Directorate of Education, he should be received at the Imperial College with full honors befitting the host.
units.literal: When Mian had been in office about ten days and Chao'en entered the directorate, the prefectural clerks made a request in advance; Mian said, "The army-observing commissioner who supervises the Directorate of Education—Mian awaits him at the Imperial College; the commissioner should generously provide the host's rites.

units.zh: 勉忝京尹，軍容倘惠顧府廷，豈敢不具蔬饌。」
units.en: As metropolitan governor I would be unworthy if he did not visit my yamen; but should he deign to come to the prefectural offices, I would of course provide a meal—nothing more."
units.literal: Mian, unworthy as metropolitan governor—if the commissioner should graciously visit the prefectural court, how would I dare not provide vegetables and food."

units.zh: 朝恩聞而銜之，因不復至太學，勉亦尋受代。
units.en: Yu Chao'en took offense and never visited the college again. Mian was soon replaced in his post.
units.literal: Chao'en, hearing this, bore a grudge; he therefore did not again go to the Imperial College, and Mian soon afterward was replaced.

units.zh: 四年，除廣州刺史，兼嶺南節度觀察使。
units.en: In the fourth year he was appointed prefect of Guangzhou and military governor and observation commissioner of Lingnan.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed prefect of Guangzhou and concurrently military governor and observation commissioner of Lingnan.

units.zh: 番禺賊帥馮崇道、桂州叛將硃濟時等阻洞為亂，前後累歲，陷沒十餘州。
units.en: The bandit leaders Feng Chongdao of Panyu and the Gui Prefecture rebel Zhu Jishi and others held the mountain passes and rebelled. For years they had overrun more than ten prefectures.
units.literal: The bandit chiefs of Panyu, Feng Chongdao, and the Gui Prefecture rebel Zhu Jishi and others blocked the mountain passes and raised disorder; for years in succession more than ten prefectures were overrun.

units.zh: 勉至，遣將李觀與容州刺史王翃人並力招討，悉斬之，五嶺平。
units.en: On arriving, Mian sent the general Li Guan and Rongzhou prefect Wang Hong to campaign together against them. All were executed and the Five Ridges were pacified.
units.literal: When Mian arrived, he sent the general Li Guan and Rongzhou prefect Wang Hong to join forces in recruiting and suppressing them; all were beheaded and the Five Ridges were pacified.

units.zh: 前後西域舶泛海至者歲才四五，勉性廉潔，舶來都不檢閱，故末年至者四十餘。
units.en: In earlier years only four or five Western merchant ships reached port each year. Mian was incorruptible by nature and never inspected incoming vessels, so that in his last year more than forty ships arrived.
units.literal: Before and after, Western Region ships that crossed the sea to arrive numbered only four or five a year; Mian by nature was incorrupt, and when ships came he did not inspect them at all; therefore in his final year more than forty arrived.

units.zh: 在官累年，器用車服無增飾。
units.en: Throughout his years in office he added no ornament to his furnishings, carriage, or dress.
units.literal: Through many years in office, his utensils, carriage, and robes received no added ornament.

units.zh: 及代歸，至石門停舟，悉搜家人所貯南貨犀象諸物，投之江中，耆老以為可繼前朝宋璟、盧奐、李朝隱之徒。
units.en: When he left office and returned north, he moored at Shimen, gathered every piece of southern treasure—ivory, rhinoceros horn, and the like—that his household had accumulated, and threw it all into the river. The elders held that he could stand beside such paragons of integrity as Song Jing, Lu Huan, and Li Chaoyin of the previous reign.
units.literal: When he was replaced and returned, at Shimen he moored his boat, searched out all the southern goods, rhinoceros horn, ivory, and other things his household had stored, and cast them into the river; the elders thought he could follow in the line of Song Jing, Lu Huan, and Li Chaoyin of the former dynasty.

units.zh: 人吏詣闕請立碑，代宗許之。
units.en: Local officials petitioned the throne for a commemorative stele, and Emperor Daizong approved.
units.literal: Officials and clerks went to the court to request that a stele be erected; Emperor Daizong granted it.

units.zh: 十年，拜工部尚書。
units.en: In the tenth year he was appointed minister of works.
units.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed minister of works.

units.zh: 及滑亳永平軍節度令狐彰卒，遺表舉勉自代，因除之。
units.en: When Linghu Zhang, military governor of the Huai-Bo-Yongping circuit, died, his final memorial recommended Mian as his successor, and Mian was appointed in his place.
units.literal: When Huai-Bo Yongping Circuit military governor Linghu Zhang died, his final memorial recommended Mian to replace him, and he was accordingly appointed.

units.zh: 在鎮八年，以舊德清重，不嚴而理，東諸侯雖暴驁者，亦宗敬之。
units.en: He governed the command for eight years. His long-standing moral authority brought order without harshness, and even the most unruly eastern warlords treated him with respect.
units.literal: In the command for eight years, by old virtue he was pure and weighty; without severity there was order; even among the eastern feudatories those who were violent and proud revered him.

units.zh: 十一年，汴宋留後田神玉卒，詔加勉汴州刺史、汴宋節度使。
units.en: In the eleventh year Tian Shenyu, acting military governor of Bian-Song, died. An edict appointed Mian prefect of Bian and military governor of Bian-Song.
units.literal: In the eleventh year Bian-Song acting military governor Tian Shenyu died; an edict additionally made Mian prefect of Bianzhou and military governor of Bian-Song.

units.zh: 未行，汴州將李靈曜阻兵，北結田承嗣，承嗣使侄悅將銳兵戍之。
units.en: Before Mian could take up the post, the Bianzhou general Li Lingyao rebelled and allied himself with Tian Chengsi to the north. Chengsi sent his nephew Tian Yue with elite troops to hold the city.
units.literal: Before he set out, the Bianzhou general Li Lingyao obstructed with arms, joined in the north with Tian Chengsi, and Chengsi sent his nephew Yue to lead crack troops to garrison the place.

units.zh: 詔勉與李忠臣、馬燧等攻討，大破之，悅僅以身免。
units.en: An edict ordered Mian, Li Zhongchen, Ma Sui, and others to attack them. The rebels were routed and Tian Yue barely escaped with his life.
units.literal: An edict ordered Mian, together with Li Zhongchen, Ma Sui, and others, to attack and suppress them; they inflicted a great defeat, and Yue barely escaped with his life.

units.zh: 靈曜北走，勉騎將杜如江擒之以獻，代宗褒賞甚厚。
units.en: Li Lingyao fled north, but Mian's cavalry officer Du Rujiang captured him and presented him as a prisoner. Emperor Daizong rewarded Mian handsomely.
units.literal: Lingyao fled north; Mian's cavalry general Du Rujiang seized him and presented him captive; Daizong rewarded him very generously.

units.zh: 既而李忠臣代鎮汴州，而勉仍舊鎮。
units.en: Li Zhongchen was then assigned to garrison Bianzhou while Mian remained at his original command.
units.literal: Shortly afterward Li Zhongchen replaced him in garrisoning Bianzhou, while Mian remained at his former command.

units.zh: 忠臣遇下貪虐，明年為麾下所逐，詔復加勉汴宋節度使，移理汴州，餘並如故。
units.en: Zhongchen governed with greed and cruelty and was driven out by his own troops the following year. An edict restored Mian as military governor of Bian-Song and transferred his headquarters to Bianzhou; his other titles remained unchanged.
units.literal: Zhongchen treated his subordinates with greed and cruelty; the next year he was driven out by his own troops; an edict again made Mian military governor of Bian-Song, transferred his administration to Bianzhou, and left the rest as before.

units.zh: 德宗嗣位，加檢校吏部尚書，尋加平章事。
units.en: When Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne, Mian was made acting minister of personnel and soon appointed chief councilor.
units.literal: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, Mian was made acting minister of personnel; soon he was made chief councilor.

units.zh: 建中元年，檢校左僕射，充河南汴宋滑亳河陽等道都統，餘如故。
units.en: In 780 he was made acting left vice director and supreme commander of the Henan, Bian-Song, Hua-Bo, He-Yang, and related circuits, with his other posts unchanged.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong he was made acting left vice director and appointed supreme commander of Henan, Bian-Song, Hua-Bo, He-Yang, and other circuits; the rest remained as before.

units.zh: 四年，李希烈反，以他盜為名，悉眾來寇汴州。
units.en: In 783 Li Xilie rebelled. Rallying under another rebel's banner, he led his full army against Bianzhou.
units.literal: In the fourth year Li Xilie rebelled; under the name of another bandit he led his entire force to invade Bianzhou.

units.zh: 勉城守累月，救援莫至，謂其將曰：「希烈兇逆殘酷，若與較力，必多殺無辜，吾不忍也。」
units.en: Mian held the city for months, but no relief came. He told his generals, "Xilie is savage and cruel. If we fight him head on, countless innocents will die. I cannot bring myself to do that."
units.literal: Mian defended the city for months; relief did not arrive; he said to his generals, "Xilie is vicious, rebellious, and cruel; if we match strength with him, many innocents will surely be killed—I cannot bear it."

units.zh: 遂潛師潰圍，南奔宋州。
units.en: He secretly led his troops out through the siege lines and fled south to Songzhou.
units.literal: He then secretly led his troops in breaking the encirclement and fled south to Songzhou.

units.zh: 詔以司徒平章事征。
units.en: An edict recalled him to court as minister of education and chief councilor.
units.literal: An edict summoned him as minister of education and chief councilor.

units.zh: 既至朝廷，素服請罪，優詔復其位，勉引過備位而已。
units.en: On reaching court he appeared in plain dress to accept blame. A gracious edict restored his rank, and Mian simply acknowledged his fault and resumed his seat.
units.literal: When he reached court he wore plain robes to request punishment; a gracious edict restored his position; Mian merely acknowledged fault and filled his seat.

units.zh: 無何，盧杞自新州員外司馬除澧州刺史，給事中袁高以杞邪佞蠹政，貶未塞責，停詔執表，遂授澧州別駕。
units.en: Before long Lu Qi was appointed from acting chief secretary of Xin Prefecture to prefect of Li. Attendant Yuan Gao argued that Qi was corrupt and destructive and that demotion to a prefecture was insufficient punishment. He blocked the edict and submitted a memorial, and Qi was reduced to vice prefect of Li instead.
units.literal: Before long Lu Qi was appointed from Xinzhou acting chief secretary to prefect of Li; the attendant Yuan Gao, on the grounds that Qi was wicked, fawning, and a plague on government, held that the demotion did not satisfy accountability, stopped the edict and presented a memorial, and Qi was then made vice prefect of Li.

units.zh: 他日，上謂勉曰：「眾人皆言盧杞奸邪，朕何不知！
units.en: On another occasion the emperor said to Mian, "Everyone says Lu Qi is treacherous and corrupt. Do you think I do not know it?
units.literal: Another day the emperor said to Mian, "Everyone says Lu Qi is wicked and treacherous—how would I not know!

units.zh: 卿知其狀乎？」
units.en: Do you know what he is really like?"
units.literal: Do you know his condition?"

units.zh: 對曰：「天下皆知其奸邪，獨陛下不知，所以為奸邪也。」
units.en: Mian answered, "The whole world knows he is treacherous and corrupt. Only Your Majesty does not know it. That is precisely what makes him treacherous and corrupt."
units.literal: He replied, "All the world knows he is wicked and treacherous; only Your Majesty does not know—this is why he is wicked and treacherous."

units.zh: 時人多其正直，然自是見疏。
units.en: Contemporaries admired his frankness, but from that day he fell from favor.
units.literal: Men of the time mostly praised his uprightness, but from this he was estranged.

units.zh: 累表辭位，遂罷知政事，加太了太保。
units.en: He repeatedly asked to resign. He was removed from the chief council and appointed Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to resign his post, was removed from participation in government affairs, and was made Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 貞元四年卒，年七十二，上頗愍悼之，冊贈太傅，賻物有差，喪葬官給。
units.en: He died in 788 at the age of seventy-two. The emperor was deeply grieved and posthumously ennobled him as Grand Tutor, granted funeral gifts of appropriate rank, and provided state support for his burial.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged seventy-two; the emperor was much moved and mourned him; by patent he was posthumously made Grand Tutor; funeral gifts were graded; burial expenses were supplied by the state.

units.zh: 勉坦率素淡，好古尚奇，清廉簡易，為宗臣之表。
units.en: Mian was forthright and unpretentious, loved antiquity and valued the unusual, and lived with incorruptible simplicity. He was a model among the imperial clan.
units.literal: Mian was frank and open, plain by nature, fond of antiquity and devoted to the unusual, incorrupt, simple, and easy in manner—a model among imperial clansmen.

units.zh: 善鼓琴，好屬詩，妙知音律，能自制琴，又有巧思，
units.en: He played the zither well, enjoyed composing poetry, had a fine ear for music, could build his own instruments, and was gifted with inventive skill.
units.literal: He was skilled at playing the zither, fond of composing poetry, subtle in understanding pitch and mode, able to make zithers himself, and also possessed of ingenious ideas.

units.zh: 及在相位向二十年，祿俸皆遺親黨，身沒而無私積。
units.en: During nearly twenty years in high office, he gave away his entire salary to relatives and friends, and at his death left no private fortune.
units.literal: And while in the chancellorship for nearly twenty years, his salary and stipends were all given to kin and associates; at his death he had no private accumulation.

units.zh: 其在大官，禮賢下士，終始盡心。
units.en: In high office he honored the worthy and treated scholars with respect, devoting himself wholeheartedly from first to last.
units.literal: When he was in great office, he honored the worthy and humbled himself before scholars, from beginning to end giving his full heart.

units.zh: 以名士李巡、張參為判官，卒於幕，三歲之內，每遇宴飲，必設虛位於筵次，陳膳執酹，辭色心妻惻，論者美之。
units.en: He appointed the renowned scholars Li Xun and Zhang Can as administrative aides. When they died in his service, for three years at every banquet he set an empty place of honor, laid out food, and poured libations with heart-rending grief. Commentators praised his devotion.
units.literal: He took the eminent scholars Li Xun and Zhang Can as administrative aides; they died in his staff; within three years, whenever he met with feasting and drinking, he always set an empty seat at the place of honor, laid out food and poured libation, his words and expression heart-rending; commentators praised this.

units.zh: 或曰：「勉失守梁城，亦可貶也。」
units.en: Some said, "Mian lost Bianzhou and ought to have been demoted."
units.literal: Some said, "Mian lost and abandoned Liang City—he too could be demoted."

units.zh: 議者曰：「不然。
units.en: Others replied, "That is not so.
units.literal: Discussants said, "Not so.

units.zh: 當賊烈之始亂，其慓悍陰禍，兇焰不可當，天方厚其毒而降之罰。
units.en: When Xilie first rebelled, his ferocity and hidden malice were irresistible; Heaven itself was visiting punishment on the realm through him.
units.literal: When the bandit Xilie first rebelled, his ferocity and hidden malice, his fierce flame, could not be withstood; Heaven was then heaping his poison and sending down punishment upon him.

units.zh: 況勉應變非長，援軍莫至，又其時關輔已俶擾矣，人心已動搖矣。
units.en: Moreover Mian was not a master of crisis, no relief force came, the capital region was already in turmoil, and popular morale was collapsing.
units.literal: Moreover Mian was not long skilled in meeting change; relief armies did not arrive; moreover at that time the capital region was already in uproar and men's hearts were already shaken.

units.zh: 以文吏之才，當虎狼之隊，其全師奔宋，非量力之恥也。
units.en: A civil official facing a wolfish army—preserving his force and withdrawing to Song was not a failure to know his limits but a prudent choice.
units.literal: With the talent of a civil official to face a pack of tigers and wolves, that he preserved his army intact and fled to Song was not the shame of misjudging his strength.

units.zh: 與其坐受喪敗，不猶愈乎！」
units.en: Better that than sitting still to be destroyed."
units.literal: Compared with sitting still to receive defeat and ruin, was it not rather better!"

units.zh: 李皋，字子蘭，曹王明玄孫，嗣王戢之子。
units.en: Li Gao, whose courtesy name was Zilan, was a great-great-grandson of Li Ming, Prince of Cao, and son of Li Ji, the succeeding prince.
units.literal: Li Gao, styled Zilan, was a great-great-grandson of Li Ming, Prince of Cao, and son of Li Ji, the succeeding prince.

units.zh: 少補左司御率府兵曹參軍。
units.en: In youth he was appointed military staff officer in the Left Bureau of the Princely Guard Command.
units.literal: In youth he was appointed military staff officer of the Left Bureau of the Princely Guard Command.

units.zh: 天寶十一載嗣封授都水使者，三遷至秘書少監，皆同正。
units.en: In 752, upon inheriting his princely title, he was appointed commissioner of waterways. After three promotions he reached acting vice director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianbao, on succeeding to the fief he was appointed commissioner of waterways; after three promotions he reached vice director of the Secretariat, all as acting posts.

units.zh: 多智數，善因事以自便。
units.en: He was resourceful and adept at turning circumstances to his advantage.
units.literal: He had much craft and stratagem and was skilled at turning affairs to his own convenience.

units.zh: 奉太妃鄭氏以孝聞。
units.en: He was known for filial devotion to his mother, Imperial Consort Dowager Lady Zheng.
units.literal: He served the imperial consort dowager Lady Zheng and was known for filial piety.

units.zh: 上元初，京師旱，米斗直數千，死者甚多。
units.en: At the beginning of the Shangyuan era the capital suffered drought. Grain sold for thousands of cash per dou and deaths were widespread.
units.literal: At the beginning of Shangyuan the capital suffered drought; a dou of rice cost several thousand cash; the dead were very many.

units.zh: 皋度俸不足養，亟請外官，不允，乃故抵微法，貶溫州長史。
units.en: Gao found his salary insufficient to support his household and repeatedly asked for an outside post. When refused, he deliberately committed a minor offense and was demoted to chief secretary of Wenzhou.
units.literal: Gao estimated that his stipend was insufficient to support his household and urgently requested an outside post; it was not granted; he then deliberately incurred a minor offense and was demoted to chief secretary of Wenzhou.

units.zh: 無幾，攝行州事。
units.en: Before long he was acting prefect.
units.literal: Before long he acted in administering the prefecture.

units.zh: 歲儉，州有官粟數十萬斛，皋欲行賑救，掾吏叩頭乞候上旨，皋曰：「夫人日不再食，當死，安暇稟命！
units.en: In a year of famine the prefecture held several hundred thousand hu of government grain. Gao wished to distribute relief, but his clerks kowtowed and begged him to await imperial approval. Gao said, "When people cannot eat twice a day they die. Where is the time to wait for orders from above?
units.literal: The year was lean; the prefecture had several hundred thousand hu of official grain; Gao wished to carry out relief; the clerks kowtowed begging to await imperial command; Gao said, "When people cannot eat twice a day they will die—where is the leisure to report for orders!

units.zh: 若殺我一身，活數千人命，利莫大焉。」
units.en: If my death saves thousands of lives, no gain could be greater."
units.literal: If killing my one person saves the lives of several thousand people, the benefit could not be greater."

units.zh: 於是開倉盡散之，以擅貸之罪，飛章自劾。
units.en: He opened the granaries and distributed the grain. He then sent an urgent memorial impeaching himself for unauthorized distribution of state grain.
units.literal: Thereupon he opened the granaries and distributed all of it; on the charge of unauthorized lending he sent an urgent memorial impeaching himself.

units.zh: 天子聞而嘉之，答以優詔，就加少府監。
units.en: The emperor commended him and replied with a gracious edict, promoting him on the spot to director of the Palace Workshops.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven heard and commended him, replied with a gracious edict, and on the spot promoted him to director of the Palace Workshops.

units.zh: 皋行縣，見一媼垂白而泣，哀而問之，對曰：「李氏之婦，有二子：鈞、鍔，宦游二十年不歸，貧無以自給。」
units.en: While touring the counties Gao saw a white-haired old woman weeping. Moved to pity, he asked her story. She said, "I am a widow of the Li family. My two sons, Jun and E, have been away in office for twenty years without returning. I am too poor to support myself."
units.literal: Gao was touring the counties and saw an old woman with white hair weeping; he pitied her and questioned her; she replied, "I am a woman of the Li family; I have two sons, Jun and E, who have been away in official service for twenty years without returning; I am poor and cannot support myself."

units.zh: 時鈞為殿中侍御史，鍔為京兆府法曹，俱以文藝登科，名重於時。
units.en: At the time Li Jun served as attendant censor and Li E as legal officer in the metropolitan government of Jingzhao. Both had passed the civil examinations on literary merit and enjoyed high reputations.
units.literal: At the time Jun was attendant censor and E was legal officer of the metropolitan prefecture of Jingzhao; both had passed the examinations through literary accomplishment and were weighty in reputation in their time.

units.zh: 皋曰：「『入則孝，出則悌，行有餘力，然後可以學文。』
units.en: Gao said, "The Analects teach: 'At home be filial, abroad be respectful; only when there is strength to spare may one study the arts.'
units.literal: Gao said, "'Entering home one is filial; going forth one is respectful to elders; when in conduct there is surplus strength, then one may study the literary arts.'

units.zh: 若二子者，豈可備於列位！」
units.en: Men such as these have no place in public office!"
units.literal: Men like these two—how can they be fitted among the ranks of office!"

units.zh: 由是舉奏，並除名勿齒。
units.en: He memorialized against them, and both were struck from the rolls and expelled from office.
units.literal: Thereupon he memorialized and impeached them; both were struck from the rolls and not counted among officials.

units.zh: 改處州別駕，行州事，以良政聞。
units.en: He was transferred to vice prefect of Chu and acted as prefect, earning a reputation for good government.
units.literal: He was changed to vice prefect of Chuzhou and administered the prefecture; he was known for good government.

units.zh: 征至京，未召見，因上書言理道，拜衡州刺史。
units.en: Summoned to the capital, he memorialized on principles of governance before being received in audience and was appointed prefect of Heng.
units.literal: Summoned to the capital, before he was granted audience he memorialized on the Way of governance and was appointed prefect of Hengzhou.

units.zh: 坐小法，貶潮州刺史。
units.en: He committed a minor offense and was demoted to prefect of Chao.
units.literal: He incurred a minor offense and was demoted to prefect of Chaozhou.

units.zh: 時楊炎謫官道州，知皋事直，及為相，復拜衡州。
units.en: Yang Yan was then in exile in Daozhou and knew Gao to be upright. When Yang became chief minister, Gao was restored to Heng.
units.literal: At the time Yang Yan was demoted to an office in Daozhou and knew that Gao's conduct was upright; when he became chief minister, Gao was again appointed to Hengzhou.

units.zh: 初，皋為御史覆訊，懼貽太妃憂，竟出則素服，入則公服，言貌如平常，太妃竟不知。
units.en: Earlier, when Gao served as censor investigating a case, he feared distressing his mother. He wore plain dress when he left home and official dress when he entered, speaking and appearing as usual, so that she never learned of his troubles.
units.literal: Earlier, when Gao as censor conducted a reinvestigation, he feared to bring worry to the imperial consort dowager; when he went out he wore plain robes, when he entered official robes, his words and appearance as usual—the consort dowager to the end did not know.

units.zh: 及為潮州，詭詞謂遷，至是復位，方泣以白，且言非疾不敢有聞。
units.en: When he was sent to Chao he told her it was a promotion. Only when he was restored to Heng did he weep and tell her the truth, saying he had concealed bad news lest she worry unless he were ill.
units.literal: When he was made prefect of Chaozhou he used deceptive words saying it was a transfer; when he now regained his post, he wept as he informed her, and said that unless ill he dared not let her hear of it.

units.zh: 建中元年，遷湖南觀察使。
units.en: In 780 he was appointed observation commissioner of Hunan.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong he was transferred to observation commissioner of Hunan.

units.zh: 前使辛京杲貪殘，有將王國良鎮邵州武岡縣，豪富，京杲以死罪加之。
units.en: His predecessor Xin Jinggao was greedy and cruel. A general named Wang Guoliang garrisoned Wugang County in Shao Prefecture and was wealthy and powerful. Jinggao condemned him to death on trumped-up charges.
units.literal: The previous commissioner Xin Jinggao was greedy and cruel; there was a general Wang Guoliang garrisoning Wugang County in Shaozhou, wealthy and powerful; Jinggao imposed the death penalty on him.

units.zh: 國良危懼，因人所苦，遂散財聚眾據縣以叛，諸道同討，聯歲不能下。
units.en: Terrified, Wang Guoliang rallied popular grievances, distributed his wealth to raise followers, seized the county, and rebelled. Troops from several circuits campaigned against him for years without success.
units.literal: Guoliang was in peril and fear; because of what people suffered, he then dispersed wealth and gathered a multitude, seized the county and rebelled; the various circuits jointly attacked, and for successive years could not subdue him.

units.zh: 皋授命日，乃曰：「驅疲甿，誅反側，非所以奉聖朝事。」
units.en: On the day Li Gao received his commission, he declared, "Driving exhausted commoners to war and executing rebels is no way to serve the sacred court."
units.literal: On the day Gao received his commission, he said: "Driving exhausted peasants and executing rebels is not the way to serve the sagely court."

units.zh: 遣使遺國良書曰；
units.en: He sent a messenger with a letter to Wang Guoliang:
units.literal: He sent a messenger to deliver a letter to Guoliang, saying;

units.zh: 「觀將軍非敢大逆，蓋遭讒嫉，救誤死而已。
units.en: "I can see that you, General, never intended outright treason. You were the victim of slander and envy, and acted only to save yourself from an unjust death.
units.literal: "I see that the general does not dare great treason—he has merely suffered slander and jealousy, saving himself from wrongful death, that is all.

units.zh: 將軍遇我，何不速降？
units.en: If you come to terms with me, why not surrender at once?
units.literal: If the general meets with me, why not surrender quickly?

units.zh: 我與將軍同為辛京杲所構，我已蒙聖朝昭雪，使我何心持刃殺將軍耶！
units.en: Both of us were framed by Xin Jinggao. I have already been vindicated by the court—how could I bear to take up arms against you!
units.literal: The general and I were both framed by Xin Jinggao; I have already been cleared by the sagely court—what heart would make me hold a blade and kill the general!

units.zh: 將軍以為不然，我以陣術破將軍陣，以攻法屠將軍城，非將軍所度也。」
units.en: If you disagree, I will break your battle lines with my tactics and raze your city with siegecraft—something you have not accounted for."
units.literal: If the general thinks otherwise, I will break the general's formation with battle tactics and slaughter the general's city with assault methods—this is not what the general anticipates."

units.zh: 國良捧書，且憂且喜，遣使請降，亦未必決。
units.en: Wang Guoliang read the letter with mingled anxiety and relief. He sent envoys offering surrender, but had not yet made up his mind.
units.literal: Guoliang received the letter in his hands, both worried and pleased; he sent a messenger to request surrender, yet was not necessarily decided.

units.zh: 皋即日赴縣受降，中道有候騎馳告曰：「國良軍中有變，言降是詐也。」
units.en: That same day Li Gao set out for the county seat to accept the surrender. Midway, scouts galloped up with word: "There is trouble in Wang Guoliang's camp—the surrender is a trick."
units.literal: That same day Gao went to the county to accept the surrender; midway there scouts galloped to report: "There is a disturbance in Guoliang's army—the surrender is said to be a ruse."

units.zh: 皋曰：「非爾輩所知。」
units.en: Li Gao said, "That is beyond your understanding."
units.literal: Gao said: "This is not something you people understand."

units.zh: 遂留麾下兵，單騎假稱使者，逕入國良壘中。
units.en: He left his troops behind, rode in alone disguised as an envoy, and went straight into Wang Guoliang's camp.
units.literal: He then left his troops behind, rode alone falsely claiming to be a messenger, and went straight into Guoliang's camp.

units.zh: 國良召使者入，皋遂大叫軍中曰：「有人識曹王否？
units.en: Wang Guoliang summoned the envoy inside. Li Gao then shouted through the camp, "Does anyone here know the Prince of Cao?
units.literal: Guoliang summoned the messenger in; Gao then shouted in the army camp: "Is there anyone who recognizes the Prince of Cao?

units.zh: 只我是。
units.en: I am he!
units.literal: I am he alone.

units.zh: 國良何不速降？」
units.en: Wang Guoliang, why don't you surrender at once?"
units.literal: Guoliang, why not surrender quickly?"

units.zh: 一軍愕眙不敢動。
units.en: The entire army stood frozen in shock, not daring to stir.
units.literal: The whole army stared in stunned amazement and did not dare move.

units.zh: 適有識者走至，傳呼曰：「是」。
units.en: Then a man who knew him ran forward shouting, "It is he!"
units.literal: Just then someone who recognized him ran forward and called out in relay: "It is he."

units.zh: 國良匍匐叩頭請罪。
units.en: Wang Guoliang prostrated himself and kowtowed in submission.
units.literal: Guoliang crawled prostrate and kowtowed to beg forgiveness.

units.zh: 皋執手約為兄弟，盡焚攻守之備，散倉庫，給兵士，令復農桑。
units.en: Li Gao clasped his hand and pledged brotherhood. He burned all siege works, opened the storehouses, paid off the soldiers, and sent them back to farming.
units.literal: Gao took his hand and pledged brotherhood; he burned all preparations for attack and defense, opened the storehouses, distributed to the soldiers, and ordered them to return to farming and mulberry cultivation.

units.zh: 有詔赦國良罪，賜名惟新。
units.en: An edict pardoned Wang Guoliang and bestowed on him the name Weixin ("Renewed").
units.literal: There was an edict pardoning Guoliang's crime and bestowing the name Weixin.

units.zh: 建中二年，丁母艱，奉喪至江陵。
units.en: In 781, upon his mother's death, he escorted her coffin to Jiangling.
units.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, he suffered his mother's bereavement and escorted the coffin to Jiangling.

units.zh: 會梁崇義反，乃授起復左衛大將軍，復還湖南，尋加散騎常侍李希烈反，遷江西道節度使、洪州刺史、兼御史大夫。
units.en: When Liang Chongyi rebelled, Li Gao was recalled from mourning as General of the Left Guard and sent back to Hunan; he was soon also made Regular Attendant Cavalier. When Li Xilie rebelled, he was transferred to military commissioner of the Jiangxi Circuit, prefect of Hong Prefecture, and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: It happened that Liang Chongyi rebelled; he was then appointed Left Guard Grand General recalled from mourning, and returned to Hunan; shortly thereafter he was additionally made Regular Attendant Cavalier. When Li Xilie rebelled, he was transferred to military commissioner of Jiangxi Circuit, prefect of Hong Prefecture, and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 至州，集將吏而令曰：「嘗有功未申者，別為行；
units.en: On reaching his post, he assembled his commanders and staff and announced, "Those with unreported past achievements, step forward in a separate line;
units.literal: Upon reaching the prefecture, he assembled the officers and staff and ordered: "Those who have past merit that has not been reported, form a separate row;

units.zh: 有策謀及器能堪佐軍者，別為行。」
units.en: Those with strategy or talent fit to serve the army, step forward in a separate line."
units.literal: Those who have strategy and ability fit to assist the army, form a separate row."

units.zh: 有裨將伊慎、李伯潛、劉旻皆自占，皋察其詞氣，驗其有功，悉補大將。
units.en: Subordinate generals Yi Shen, Li Boqian, and Liu Min all stepped forward. Li Gao read their bearing and verified their records, and appointed them all major generals.
units.literal: The subordinate generals Yi Shen, Li Boqian, and Liu Min all claimed places for themselves; Gao observed their words and demeanor, verified their merits, and all were appointed major generals.

units.zh: 擢王鍔委之中軍，以馬彝、許孟容為賓佐。
units.en: He promoted Wang E to command the central army and made Ma Yi and Xu Morong his chief advisers.
units.literal: He promoted Wang E and entrusted him with the central army, making Ma Yi and Xu Morong his personal aides.

units.zh: 繕甲兵，具戰艦，將軍二萬餘。
units.en: He readied armor and arms, built warships, and mustered more than twenty thousand troops.
units.literal: He repaired armor and weapons, equipped battle ships, and commanded over twenty thousand troops.

units.zh: 初，伊慎將江西兵從李希烈平襄州，及反，懼皋任之，乃陰遣遺之鎖甲，又詐為慎書往復，置遺於境。
units.en: Earlier, Yi Shen had led Jiangxi troops under Li Xilie to capture Xiang Prefecture. When Xilie rebelled, fearing Li Gao would still employ Shen, Xilie secretly sent him chain mail as a gift and forged correspondence in Shen's name, leaving the gifts at the border.
units.literal: Initially, Yi Shen had led Jiangxi troops under Li Xilie to pacify Xiang Prefecture; when Xilie rebelled, fearing that Gao would employ him, Xilie secretly sent him chain armor as a gift, and also forged letters exchanged in Shen's name, placing the gifts at the border.

units.zh: 上聞，即遣中使斬慎，皋表請捨令自效。
units.en: When the emperor heard of it, he dispatched an envoy to execute Yi Shen. Li Gao memorialized the throne asking that Shen be spared and allowed to prove his loyalty in battle.
units.literal: When the emperor heard of this, he immediately sent a court envoy to execute Shen; Gao submitted a memorial requesting that he be spared and allowed to redeem himself through service.

units.zh: 會與賊夾江為陣，中使又至，皋乃勉令以功自贖，賜之以所乘馬及器甲，令將鋒而先，皋率軍繼之，責其有功，果大破賊，斬首數百級，慎方得免罪。
units.en: Just then they drew up against the enemy on opposite banks of the river. When the envoy arrived again, Li Gao urged Shen to win redemption through merit, gave him his own horse and armor, and sent him at the head of the vanguard while he followed with the main force. Shen broke the enemy soundly, taking several hundred heads, and only then escaped punishment.
units.literal: It happened that they faced the rebels across the river in battle formation; the court envoy came again; Gao then urged Shen to redeem himself through merit, gifted him his own mount and armor, ordered him to lead the vanguard, Gao followed with the army and required him to achieve merit; they indeed routed the rebels greatly, beheading several hundred; only then did Shen escape punishment.

units.zh: 賊樹堡柵於蔡山，皋度峻險不可攻，乃聲言西取蘄州，理戰艦，分兵傍南涯，與舟師溯江而上。
units.en: The rebels fortified Cai Mountain. Judging the heights too steep to assault directly, Li Gao announced a march on Qi Prefecture to the west, fitted out warships, sent troops along the south bank, and sailed upstream with his fleet.
units.literal: The rebels built fortifications and palisades at Cai Mountain; Gao judged the terrain steep and perilous and impossible to attack; he then proclaimed he would take Qi Prefecture to the west, prepared battle ships, divided troops along the southern bank, and with the naval force sailed upriver.

units.zh: 賊以老弱守柵，引軍循江隨戰艦，南北與皋兵相直。
units.en: The rebels left the weak to hold the fort and marched their main force downstream alongside the warships, drawing up north and south opposite Li Gao's army.
units.literal: The rebels left the aged and weak to guard the palisades and led their army along the river following the warships; north and south they faced Gao's troops directly.

units.zh: 去蔡山三百餘里，皋令步兵登舟，順流東下，不日拔蔡山。
units.en: Three hundred-odd li downstream from Cai Mountain, Li Gao put his infantry aboard ship and swept downstream. Within days they took Cai Mountain.
units.literal: Over three hundred li from Cai Mountain, Gao ordered the infantry to board ships and float downstream to the east; within days they captured Cai Mountain.

units.zh: 賊還救，間一日方至，大破之，因進拔蘄州，降其將李良，又取黃州，斬首千餘，兵益振，舒王為元帥，加皋前軍兵馬使。
units.en: The enemy turned back to relieve the mountain but arrived a day too late. Li Gao routed them, took Qi Prefecture, and accepted the surrender of the rebel general Li Liang. He also captured Huang Prefecture, taking more than a thousand heads, and his army's morale soared. With the Prince of Shu as overall commander, Li Gao was made forward-army commissioner.
units.literal: The rebels returned to rescue; only after one day's interval did they arrive; he routed them greatly, then advanced to capture Qi Prefecture, accepting the surrender of their general Li Liang, also took Huang Prefecture, beheaded over a thousand; the army's momentum grew; the Prince of Shu served as commander-in-chief, and Gao was additionally made forward-army commissioner of horses and troops.

units.zh: 德宗居奉天，淮南節度陳少游強取鹽鐵錢，其使包佶以財幣溯江，次於蘄口。
units.en: While Emperor Dezong was at Fengtian, Chen Shaoyou, military commissioner of Huainan, forcibly seized salt-and-iron revenues. The envoy Bao Ji sailed upriver with the treasury goods and halted at Qikou.
units.literal: Emperor Dezong stayed at Fengtian; Chen Shaoyou, military commissioner of Huainan, forcibly seized the salt and iron funds; his envoy Bao Ji with wealth and goods sailed upriver and stopped at Qikou.

units.zh: 時希烈已屠汴州，又遣驍將杜少誠將步騎萬餘來寇蘄、黃，將絕江道。
units.en: Li Xilie had already sacked Bian Prefecture and now sent the fierce general Du Shaocheng with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry against Qi and Huang, aiming to sever the river route.
units.literal: At that time Xilie had already slaughtered Bian Prefecture; he also sent his fierce general Du Shaocheng leading over ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Qi and Huang, intending to cut the river route.

units.zh: 皋遣伊慎將七千眾御之，遇於永安戍。
units.en: Li Gao sent Yi Shen with seven thousand men to oppose them. They met at Yong'an garrison.
units.literal: Gao sent Yi Shen leading seven thousand troops to resist them; they met at Yong'an garrison.

units.zh: 慎列三柵，相去才四里，列鼓角中柵。
units.en: Yi Shen set three camps four li apart and stationed drums and horns in the center camp.
units.literal: Shen arranged three palisades, only four li apart, and placed drums and horns in the central palisade.

units.zh: 少誠至，分兵圍之，部隊未嚴，聲鼓而三柵齊出奮擊，不為行陣，賊亂，少誠敗走，斬首萬級，封屍為京觀。
units.en: Du Shaocheng arrived and sent detachments to encircle the camps before his lines were fully set. At the blast of the drums all three camps charged at once in a headlong assault. The rebels broke, Du Shaocheng fled, and ten thousand heads were taken. The bodies were heaped into a victory mound.
units.literal: Shaocheng arrived, divided troops to surround them; the formations were not yet set; at the sounding of drums all three palisades sallied forth and struck vigorously, without forming battle lines; the rebels were disorderly; Shaocheng fled in defeat; ten thousand heads were beheaded; the corpses were piled into a victory mound.

units.zh: 以功加銀青光祿大夫，進封五百戶。
units.en: For this achievement he was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and granted an additional five hundred tax households.
units.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and his fief was increased by five hundred households.

units.zh: 上至梁州，進獻繼至。
units.en: When the emperor moved to Liang Prefecture, Li Gao's contributions of supplies kept arriving.
units.literal: The emperor went to Liang Prefecture; tribute presentations continued to arrive.

units.zh: 皋以上蒙塵於外，不敢居城府，乃於西塞山上游大洲屯軍，從近縣為軍市，商貨畢至。
units.en: Because the emperor was in exile, Li Gao did not feel it fitting to occupy the prefectural seat. He encamped on Great Isle upstream on Mount Xisai, set up army markets with neighboring counties, and merchants flocked there.
units.literal: Because the emperor above was dust-stained abroad, Gao did not dare dwell in the prefecture city; he then stationed troops on Great Isle upstream on Mount Xisai, established military markets from nearby counties, and merchants and goods all arrived.

units.zh: 加工部尚書。
units.en: He was additionally appointed Minister of Works.
units.literal: He was additionally made Minister of Works.

units.zh: 駕還京師，又遣伊慎、王鍔將兵圍安州，州城阻□水為固，攻之累日不下。
units.en: After the emperor returned to the capital, Li Gao again sent Yi Shen and Wang E to besiege An Prefecture. The city was strongly defended by the Ru River, and the siege dragged on for days without success.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, he again sent Yi Shen and Wang E leading troops to besiege An Prefecture; the prefectural city was fortified by the Ru River; they attacked for many days without capturing it.

units.zh: 希烈遣甥劉戒虛將步八千來援。
units.en: Li Xilie sent his nephew Liu Jiexu with eight thousand foot soldiers to relieve the city.
units.literal: Xilie sent his nephew Liu Jiexu leading eight thousand infantry as relief.

units.zh: 皋命李伯潛分師迎擊於應山，獲戒虛及大將二、裨將二十，斬首千餘。
units.en: Li Gao ordered Li Boqian to take a detachment and intercept them at Yingshan. They captured Liu Jiexu, two major generals, and twenty subordinate commanders, taking more than a thousand heads.
units.literal: Gao ordered Li Boqian to divide forces and intercept at Yingshan; they captured Jiexu and two major generals and twenty subordinate generals, beheading over a thousand.

units.zh: 面縛戒虛等之城下，乃使人說之，賊曰：「得大將及賓佐一二人為信，當降。」
units.en: Li Gao paraded Jiexu and the others bound before the walls and sent envoys to negotiate. The defenders replied, "Give us one or two senior commanders or staff officers as hostages, and we will surrender."
units.literal: With Jiexu and others bound facing outward at the foot of the city wall, he then sent someone to persuade them; the rebels said: "If we receive one or two major generals and staff members as pledge, we will surrender."

units.zh: 皋乃使王鍔、馬彝繩城而入，城中大呼，乃出降。
units.en: Li Gao sent Wang E and Ma Yi over the wall on ropes. The city erupted in cheers, and the garrison surrendered.
units.literal: Gao then had Wang E and Ma Yi climb the wall by rope and enter; the city shouted loudly, and then they came out to surrender.

units.zh: 希烈又遣兵援隨州，皋令伊慎擊於厲鄉，大破之，復平靜、白雁等關。
units.en: Li Xilie sent another force to relieve Suizhou. Li Gao ordered Yi Shen to strike at Lixiang, routed them thoroughly, and recaptured Jing Pass, Baiyan Pass, and the other strongpoints.
units.literal: Xilie again sent troops to relieve Suizhou; Gao ordered Yi Shen to attack at Lixiang, routing them greatly, and again pacified Jing, Baiyan, and other passes.

units.zh: 希烈懼，乃戢兵。
units.en: Li Xilie was cowed and held his army back.
units.literal: Xilie was afraid and then restrained his troops.

units.zh: 貞元初，拜江陵尹、荊南節度等使，江漢倚皋為固。
units.en: At the start of the Zhenyuan era, he was made magistrate of Jiangling and military commissioner of Jingnan. The Jiang and Han regions depended on him as their mainstay.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, he was appointed magistrate of Jiangling, military commissioner of Jingnan and related posts; Jiang and Han relied on Gao as their bulwark.

units.zh: 未幾，李思登以隨州降。
units.en: Before long, Li Sideng surrendered Suizhou to him.
units.literal: Before long, Li Sideng surrendered Suizhou.

units.zh: 凡下州四、縣十七，大小十餘陣，未嘗敗衄。
units.en: In all he took four prefectures and seventeen counties in more than ten battles, large and small, without ever suffering a defeat.
units.literal: In all he captured four prefectures and seventeen counties, fought more than ten engagements large and small, and never suffered defeat.

units.zh: 淮西既平，請護喪祔東都，上遣中使吊，贈父右僕射，母曹國太妃。
units.en: After Huai West was pacified, he petitioned to escort his parents' remains for burial in the Eastern Capital. The emperor sent an envoy to offer condolences, posthumously ennobling his father as Right Vice Director and his mother as Princess of Caoguo.
units.literal: Once Huai West was pacified, he requested to escort the coffin for burial alongside the Eastern Capital; the emperor sent a court envoy to offer condolences; his father was posthumously given Right Vice Director, his mother Princess of Caoguo.

units.zh: 葬畢來朝，詔還鎮，出東都以拜墓，觀者榮之。
units.en: After the funeral he came to court. Ordered back to his post, he paid his respects at the tombs as he left the Eastern Capital, to the admiration of all who saw him.
units.literal: After the burial was completed he came to court; an edict ordered him back to his post; passing out of the Eastern Capital to visit the tombs, onlookers regarded him with honor.

units.zh: 先，江陵東北有廢田傍漢古堤二處，每夏則溢，皋始命塞之，廣田五千頃，畝得一鐘。
units.en: Previously, northeast of Jiangling lay abandoned farmland beside two ancient Han-era dikes that flooded every summer. Li Gao had them repaired and reclaimed five thousand qing of fields, each mu yielding a full zhong of grain.
units.literal: Previously, northeast of Jiangling there were abandoned fields beside two ancient Han dykes; every summer they overflowed; Gao first ordered them blocked, expanding fields to five thousand qing; each mu yielded one zhong.

units.zh: 規江南廢洲為廬捨，架江為二橋，流人自占二千餘戶。
units.en: He laid out abandoned river islands south of the Yangtze for housing, built two bridges across the river, and more than two thousand displaced families settled there on their own.
units.literal: He planned abandoned islets south of the river as dwellings, built two bridges spanning the river, and over two thousand refugee households settled themselves.

units.zh: 自荊至樂鄉凡二百里，旅舍鄉聚凡十數，大者皆數百家。
units.en: From Jingzhou to Lexiang, two hundred li of road, he established more than a dozen inns and market towns, the largest numbering several hundred households each.
units.literal: From Jing to Lexiang altogether two hundred li, inns and village clusters totaled more than ten; the larger ones each had several hundred households.

units.zh: 楚俗佻薄，不穿井，飲陂澤，皋始命合錢開井以便人。
units.en: The people of Chu were careless about sanitation—they dug no wells and drank from ponds and marshes. Li Gao organized collective funds to dig wells for public use.
units.literal: Chu custom was frivolous and shallow; they did not dig wells and drank from ponds and marshes; Gao first ordered pooled funds to dig wells for people's convenience.

units.zh: 初平希烈，吳少誠殺陳仙奇，上以襄、鄧要厄，三年，除襄州刺史、山南東道節度等使，割汝、隨隸焉。
units.en: After Li Xilie was subdued, Wu Shaocheng murdered Chen Xianqi. Considering Xiang and Deng strategic passes, in 787 the court appointed Li Gao prefect of Xiang Prefecture and military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, attaching Ru and Suizhou to his jurisdiction.
units.literal: When Xilie was first pacified, Wu Shaocheng killed Chen Xianqi; the emperor considered Xiang and Deng strategic choke points; in the third year, he was appointed prefect of Xiang Prefecture, military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit and related posts; Ru and Sui were severed and placed under his command.

units.zh: 練兵積糧，市回鶻馬益騎兵，堂大畋以教士，少誠憚之。
units.en: He trained troops, stockpiled grain, bought Uighur horses to expand his cavalry, and held great hunts to drill his men. Wu Shaocheng grew wary of him.
units.literal: He drilled troops and stockpiled grain, purchased Uighur horses to increase cavalry, and held great hunts in the hall grounds to train soldiers; Shaocheng feared him.

units.zh: 性勤儉，知人疾苦，設監司，能參聽下，持將吏短長，賞罰必信。
units.en: Diligent and frugal by nature, he understood people's hardships. He established supervisory offices, listened to reports from below, tracked his officers' strengths and failings, and always kept his word in reward and punishment.
units.literal: By nature diligent and frugal, he knew people's hardships; he established supervisory offices, was able to listen to subordinates' reports, kept track of officers' strengths and weaknesses, and rewards and punishments were always trustworthy.

units.zh: 所至常平物價，貴則出賣之，給將吏廩俸，豪家不得擅其利。
units.en: Wherever he served he stabilized grain prices, selling from stores when prices rose to pay his officers' salaries, denying powerful families any monopoly on profit.
units.literal: Wherever he went he stabilized commodity prices; when prices were high he sold grain, supplying officers' rations and salaries; powerful families could not monopolize the profit.

units.zh: 常運心巧思為戰艦，挾二輪蹈之，翔風鼓浪，疾若掛帆席，所造省易而久固。
units.en: He constantly applied his ingenuity to warship design. Powered by two paddle wheels, they rode the wind and churned the waves, swift as sails full of wind—yet cheaper to build and more durable.
units.literal: He constantly applied ingenious thought to warships; they had two wheels tread upon, riding wind and stirring waves, swift as hoisting sail cloth; what he built was economical and simple yet long-lasting and sturdy.

units.zh: 又造欹器，進入內中。
units.en: He also devised a tipping vessel and presented it to the imperial inner court.
units.literal: He also made a tipping vessel and presented it to the inner palace.

units.zh: 每遺人物，常自秤量。
units.en: Whenever he sent gifts, he weighed them himself.
units.literal: Whenever he sent gifts of goods, he always weighed them himself.

units.zh: 署之官匹帛皆印之，絕吏之私。
units.en: He stamped official shipments of cloth with his seal, shutting out embezzlement by his staff.
units.literal: All official bolts of silk he marked with seals, cutting off officials' private gain.

units.zh: 初，扶風馬彝未知名，皋始辟之，卒以正直稱。
units.en: Ma Yi of Fufeng was unknown when Li Gao first recruited him, but he came to be renowned for his integrity.
units.literal: Initially, Fufeng's Ma Yi was not yet known by name; Gao first recruited him, and in the end he was famed for upright integrity.

units.zh: 漢陽王張柬之有林園在州西，公府多假之游宴，皋將買之，彝斂衽而言曰：「張漢陽有中興功，今遺業當百代保之，王縱欲之，奈何令其子孫自鬻焉！」
units.en: The estate and garden of Prince of Hanyang Zhang Jianzhi lay west of the city, and the government often borrowed it for banquets. When Li Gao was about to purchase it, Ma Yi straightened his robes and said, "Zhang of Hanyang restored the dynasty. His family holding should be preserved for generations. Even if Your Highness desires it, how can you have his descendants sell their own heritage!"
units.literal: Prince of Hanyang Zhang Jianzhi had an estate and garden west of the prefecture; the government offices often borrowed it for banquets; Gao was about to buy it; Yi gathered his robes and spoke: "Zhang of Hanyang had merit in restoring the dynasty; his remaining estate ought to be preserved for a hundred generations—though the prince may desire it, how can he let his descendants sell it themselves!"

units.zh: 皋謝曰：「主吏失詞，為足下羞；
units.en: Li Gao apologized, "My staff misspoke and brought shame upon you;
units.literal: Gao apologized: "The chief clerk misspoke—this shames you before your guest;

units.zh: 微足下，安得聞此言！」
units.en: without you, I would never have heard such counsel!"
units.literal: without you, how could I have heard these words!"

units.zh: 以改過遷善、知人任下為己任，故賓從將佐多至大官。
units.en: He made correcting his faults, accepting good counsel, and knowing and trusting capable subordinates his personal standards, and many of his retainers and staff rose to high office.
units.literal: Taking correcting faults and advancing toward goodness and knowing people and employing subordinates as his personal charge, therefore his guests, followers, and staff assistants mostly rose to high office.

units.zh: 貞元八年三月，暴卒於位，年六十，廢朝三日，贈右僕射，賻吊有差，謚曰成。
units.en: In the third month of 792 he died suddenly in office at the age of sixty. Court mourning was observed for three days. He was posthumously ennobled as Right Vice Director, funeral gifts were sent in due measure, and he was given the posthumous name Cheng ("Accomplished").
units.literal: In the third month of the eighth year of Zhenyuan, he suddenly died in office at age sixty; court was suspended three days; he was posthumously given Right Vice Director; condolence gifts were graded; his posthumous title was Cheng.

units.zh: 子象古、道古、復古。
units.en: His sons were Li Xianggu, Li Daogu, and Li Fugu.
units.literal: His sons were Xianggu, Daogu, and Fugu.

units.zh: 象古自衡州刺史為安南都護。
units.en: Li Xianggu rose from prefect of Heng Prefecture to protector-general of Annam.
units.literal: Xianggu went from prefect of Heng Prefecture to protector-general of Annan.

units.zh: 元和十四年，為楊清所殺，妻子支黨無焦類焉。
units.en: In 819 Yang Qing murdered him. His wife, children, kinsmen, and followers were wiped out to the last person.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yuanhe, he was killed by Yang Qing; wife, children, clansmen, and followers—none escaped burning.

units.zh: 楊清者，代為南方酋豪，屬象古貪縱，人心不附，又惡清之強，自驩州刺史召為牙門將，郁郁不快。
units.en: Yang Qing came from a line of southern tribal chieftains. Li Xianggu was greedy and self-indulgent, and the people did not support him. Resenting Yang Qing's strength, he summoned him from his post as prefect of Huan Prefecture to serve as a gate guard—a slight that left Yang deeply aggrieved.
units.literal: Yang Qing was for generations a chieftain and magnate of the south; as Xianggu was greedy and indulgent, people's hearts did not attach to him; he also hated Qing's strength; from prefect of Huan Prefecture he summoned him as gate guard general, and Qing was sullen and displeased.

units.zh: 無何，邕管黃家賊叛，詔象古發兵數道共討之，像古命清領兵三千赴焉。
units.en: Before long, the Huang bandits rebelled in Yong and Guan. The court ordered Li Xianggu to attack on several fronts. Li Xianggu sent Yang Qing with three thousand men to join the campaign.
units.literal: Before long, Huang bandits rebelled in Yong and Guan; an edict ordered Xianggu to dispatch troops on several routes jointly to suppress them; Xianggu ordered Qing to lead three thousand troops to go there.

units.zh: 清與其子志烈及所親杜士交潛謀回戈，夜襲安南，數日城陷，像古故及於害。
units.en: Yang Qing, his son Zhilie, and his confidant Du Shijiao secretly plotted to turn their forces around. They struck Annam by night and took the city within days. Li Xianggu met his death in the attack.
units.literal: Qing with his son Zhilie and his intimate Du Shijiao secretly plotted to turn their spears about; by night they attacked Annan; within days the city fell; Xianggu thereby met with harm.

units.zh: 朝廷命唐州刺史桂仲武為都護，且招諭之。
units.en: The court appointed Gui Zhongwu, prefect of Tang Prefecture, as the new protector-general and sent envoys to negotiate.
units.literal: The court appointed Gui Zhongwu, prefect of Tang Prefecture, as protector-general, and also issued summons and persuasion to them.

units.zh: 赦清，以為瓊州刺史。
units.en: Yang Qing was pardoned and appointed prefect of Qiong Prefecture.
units.literal: Qing was pardoned and made prefect of Qiong Prefecture.

units.zh: 仲武至境，清不納，復約束部署，刑戮憯虐，人無聊生。
units.en: When Gui Zhongwu reached the frontier, Yang Qing refused to admit him. He tightened his grip, and his punishments grew savage until the people could barely survive.
units.literal: Zhongwu reached the border; Qing did not accept him; again he imposed discipline and deployments; punishments and executions were cruel and savage; people had no means to live.

units.zh: 仲武使人諭其酋豪，數月間，歸附繼至，約兵七千餘人，收其城，斬清及其子志貞，籍沒其家。
units.en: Gui Zhongwu won over the tribal leaders. Within months their allegiance shifted, until he mustered some seven thousand men, retook the city, executed Yang Qing and his son Zhizhen, and confiscated the family's property.
units.literal: Zhongwu sent men to persuade the chieftains and magnates; within several months submissions followed in succession; about over seven thousand troops; they recovered the city, executed Qing and his son Zhizhen, and confiscated his household property.

units.zh: 志烈與士交敗，保於長州之鑿溪，尋以所部兵來降。
units.en: Zhilie and Du Shijiao were defeated and fled to Zaoxi Creek in Chang Prefecture, then soon surrendered with the troops they still commanded.
units.literal: Zhilie and Shijiao were defeated, took refuge at Zaoxi in Chang Prefecture; shortly thereafter they came to surrender with the troops under their command.

units.zh: 道古登進士第，遷司門員外郎。
units.en: Li Daogu passed the jinshi examination and was promoted to deputy director in the Ministry of Justice.
units.literal: Daogu passed the jinshi examination and was transferred to deputy director of the Ministry of Justice's Gate office.

units.zh: 便佞巧宦，早升朝籍，常以酒餚棋博游公卿門，角賭之際，每偽為不勝而厚償之，故當時有虛名，而嗜利者悉與之狎。
units.en: Smooth, fawning, and skilled at court advancement, he rose early in official rank. He cultivated powerful men with feasts, chess, and gambling, deliberately losing wagers and paying lavishly. He enjoyed a hollow reputation, and the profit-minded all courted his friendship.
units.literal: Smooth and fawning, skilled at office; he rose early to court register; he often with wine, food, chess, and gambling visited grand ministers' doors; in contests of wagering, he always feigned defeat and paid heavily to compensate them; therefore at the time he had a hollow reputation, and those greedy for profit all became intimate with him.

units.zh: 歷處、隨、唐、睦四州刺史，由黔中觀察為鄂、岳、沔、蘄、安、黃團練觀察使，時元和十一年也。
units.en: He served as prefect of Chu, Sui, Tang, and Mu prefectures, then rose from observation commissioner of Qianzhong to training and observation commissioner over E, Yue, Mian, Qi, An, and Huang—in 816.
units.literal: He served as prefect of four prefectures—Chu, Sui, Tang, and Mu; from Qianzhong observation commissioner he became training and observation commissioner of E, Yue, Mian, Qi, An, and Huang; this was in the eleventh year of Yuanhe.

units.zh: 初，以柳公綽在鎮無功，議將代之，裴度言：「道古嗣曹王皋之子，皋嘗以江漢兵遏希烈之亂，威惠至今在人，復用其子必能繼美。」
units.en: When Liu Gongchuo's tenure had yielded no results, the court considered replacing him. Pei Du argued, "Li Daogu is the son of Prince of Cao Li Gao. Li Gao once held the Jiang-Han line against Li Xilie's rebellion, and his prestige and kindness are remembered to this day. Appointing his son would carry on that legacy."
units.literal: Initially, because Liu Gongchuo at his post had no achievements, there was discussion of replacing him; Pei Du said: "Daogu is heir as son of Prince of Cao Gao; Gao once with Jiang-Han troops checked Xi Lie's rebellion; prestige and kindness remain in people's hearts to this day; employing his son again will surely be able to continue the excellence."

units.zh: 憲宗然之，故有此授。
units.en: Emperor Xianzong agreed, and Li Daogu received the appointment.
units.literal: Emperor Xianzong approved this, and therefore there was this appointment.

units.zh: 及赴鎮，倍道而行，以數騎徑入安州城。
units.en: He rushed to his post at forced marches and rode straight into An Prefecture with only a handful of men.
units.literal: When going to his post, he traveled double marches; with several horsemen he went straight into An Prefecture city.

units.zh: 時公綽殊未意道古至，惶駭而出，家財多為所奪。
units.en: Liu Gongchuo had no warning of his arrival and fled in panic. Li Daogu seized much of his household property.
units.literal: At that time Gongchuo had no idea Daogu would arrive; he fled in panic and alarm; much household property was seized by him.

units.zh: 十二年，道古攻申州，克其羅城，乃進圍逼其中城。
units.en: In 817 Li Daogu attacked Shen Prefecture, took the outer wall, and pressed the siege of the inner citadel.
units.literal: In the twelfth year, Daogu attacked Shen Prefecture, captured its outer wall, then advanced to besiege and press the inner wall.

units.zh: 城中守卒夜帥婦人登城而呼，懸門竊發，分出其眾，道古之眾驚亂，為虜所殺。
units.en: At night the defenders sent women onto the walls to shout. They unbarred the suspended gate, sallied out in separate bands, and caught Li Daogu's troops in panicked confusion. Many were slaughtered.
units.literal: The garrison soldiers in the city by night led women up the walls to shout; the suspended gate was secretly opened; they divided and sent out their forces; Daogu's troops were alarmed and disorderly and were killed by the enemy.

units.zh: 初，李聽守安州，未嘗退衄。
units.en: When Li Ting had held An Prefecture, he had never suffered a reverse.
units.literal: Previously, Li Ting defended An Prefecture and never once suffered defeat.

units.zh: 及道古至，誣奏聽，移去之，乃自帥兵出穆陵。
units.en: When Li Daogu arrived, he brought false charges against Li Ting and had him removed, then took command of the force himself and marched out of Muleng Pass.
units.literal: When Daogu arrived, he slanderously memorialized against Ting, had him transferred away, then personally led troops out of Muleng.

units.zh: 士卒驕惰，賜給多闕，其度支供軍錢，道古半以奉權倖，半以沒己，人皆怨怒，不肯力戰。
units.en: His troops had grown proud and lax. Pay and rations fell short, and of the supply funds from the treasury Li Daogu half spent currying favor with the powerful and half pocketed for himself. The men were furious and would not fight.
units.literal: The soldiers were arrogant and slack; grants and supplies were largely lacking; of the treasury funds supplied for the army, Daogu half used to bribe powerful favorites, half embezzled for himself; all were resentful and angry and unwilling to fight hard.

units.zh: 賊亦易道古，以羸兵抵之，故道古前後再攻破申州外城而不能拔。
units.en: The rebels likewise held Li Daogu in contempt and met him with inferior troops. He twice breached the outer walls of Shen Prefecture but could never take the city.
units.literal: The rebels also looked down on Daogu; with weak troops they resisted him; therefore Daogu twice before and after broke through Shen Prefecture's outer wall yet could not capture it.

units.zh: 至李愬入蔡州，乃降。
units.en: Only after Li Su stormed Cai Prefecture did they surrender.
units.literal: When Li Su entered Cai Prefecture, then they surrendered.

units.zh: 元和十三年，入為宗正卿。
units.en: In 818 he was recalled to the capital as director of the Directorate for Imperial Clansmen.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe, he entered [the capital] as director of the Directorate for Imperial Clansmen.

units.zh: 道古在鄂州日，以貪暴聞，懼終得罪，乃薦山人柳泌以媚於上。
units.en: While at E Prefecture Li Daogu had a reputation for greed and cruelty. Fearing eventual disgrace, he recommended the mountaintop recluse Liu Bi to curry favor with the emperor.
units.literal: In Daogu's days at E Prefecture, he was known for greed and violence; fearing he would ultimately incur guilt, he recommended the mountain recluse Liu Bi to flatter the emperor.

units.zh: 後又為左金吾衛將軍。
units.en: He later served as general of the Left Jinwu Guard.
units.literal: Later he also served as general of the Left Jinwu Guard.

units.zh: 憲宗季年頗信方士，銳於服食，詔天下搜訪奇士。
units.en: In his later years Emperor Xianzong placed great faith in alchemists and eagerly pursued elixirs of immortality. He ordered an empire-wide search for wonder-workers.
units.literal: In Xianzong's late years he greatly trusted alchemical masters, was keen on ingesting elixirs; he decreed searching the empire for extraordinary men.

units.zh: 宰相皇甫鎛方諛媚固寵，道古言柳泌有道術，鎛得進之，待詔翰林。
units.en: Chief Minister Huangfu Bo was then currying favor through flattery. Daogu claimed that Liu Bi possessed Daoist arts. Bo presented him to the throne, and Liu was retained at the Hanlin Academy.
units.literal: Chief minister Huangfu Bo was then flattering to secure favor; Daogu said Liu Bi possessed the Way and its arts; Bo was able to present him, and he awaited edicts at the Hanlin Academy.

units.zh: 憲宗服餌過當，暴成狂躁之疾，以至棄代。
units.en: Emperor Xianzong took elixirs in excess and suddenly fell into violent mania, which led to his death.
units.literal: Xianzong took elixirs in excess and suddenly developed a disorder of frenzy and agitation, until he passed away.

units.zh: 穆宗在東宮，扼腕於其事，及居喪，皆竄逐誅之。
units.en: While still heir apparent, Muzong had been deeply troubled by these events. Once he assumed the throne in mourning, he banished or executed all those involved.
units.literal: Muzong, while in the Eastern Palace, wrung his hands over this affair; when he entered mourning on ascending the throne, he banished or executed them all.

units.zh: 鎛既貶責，授道古循州司馬，終以服丹藥，歐血而卒。
units.en: After Bo was demoted and punished, Daogu was appointed acting chief secretary of Xun Prefecture. He ultimately died vomiting blood from the elixirs he had taken.
units.literal: After Bo was demoted and censured, Daogu was appointed acting chief secretary of Xunzhou; in the end, because he had taken elixir drugs, he vomited blood and died.

units.zh: 【史贊】
units.en: Historian's Commendation
units.literal: Historian's Commendation

units.zh: 史臣曰：李勉、李皋，稟性端莊，處身廉潔，臨民蒞事，動有美聲，可謂宗臣之英也。
units.en: The historiographer writes: Li Mian and Li Gao were upright and dignified by nature, lived with incorruptible integrity, and in governing the people and conducting affairs always earned praise. They may truly be called the finest of the imperial clan.
units.literal: The historiographer states: Li Mian and Li Gao received upright and dignified natures, conducted themselves with incorruptible purity, and in governing the people and handling affairs always won fine repute—they may be called the finest among imperial clansmen.

units.zh: 若夫治軍旅，禦寇戎，謀必臧，戰必勝，則又勉不及皋遠矣。
units.en: In raising armies, repelling invaders, and achieving unfailing strategy and victory in battle, however, Mian fell far short of Gao.
units.literal: As for governing armies, repelling border enemies, plans always proving sound and battles always won, in this Mian fell far short of Gao.

units.zh: 道古便佞，奸以事君，何父子之不相類也。
units.en: Daogu was sycophantic and treacherous in his service to the throne. How unlike father and son the two generations were!
units.literal: Daogu was fawning and crafty, serving his lord with treachery—how unlike father and son!

units.zh: 贊曰：我宗之英，曰皋與勉，才雖不同，道豈相遠。
units.en: The commendation reads: The finest of our house are Gao and Mian. Their talents differed, yet how far apart could their moral way have been?
units.literal: The commendation states: The finest of our clan are called Gao and Mian; though their talents differ, how could their Way be far apart?

units.zh: 李希烈揣知之，上表數崇義過惡，請率先誅討。
units.en: Li Xilie divined their intent and submitted a memorial listing Chongyi's crimes, asking to take the lead in punishing him.
units.literal: Li Xilie guessed their intent and submitted a memorial listing Chongyi's faults, asking to take the lead in punishment.

units.zh: 無幾，希烈既平崇義，果有不順之跡，上思承言，故驟加擢用。
units.en: Before long Xilie had pacified Chongyi and indeed showed signs of rebellion; the emperor recalled Cheng's warning and swiftly promoted him.
units.literal: Before long Xilie had pacified Chongyi and indeed showed signs of disobedience; the emperor recalled Cheng's words and swiftly promoted him.

units.zh: 建中二年七月，拜同州刺史、河中尹、晉絳都防禦觀察使。
units.en: In the seventh month of 781 he was made prefect of Tong, mayor of the Hezhong metropolitan area, and commissioner of defense and observation for Jin and Jiang.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Jianzhong he was made Prefect of Tong, Mayor of the Hezhong metropolitan area, and Commissioner of Defense and Observation for Jin and Jiang.

units.zh: 希烈既破崇義，擁兵襄州，遂有其地。
units.en: After Xilie defeated Chongyi he massed troops at Xiangzhou and thereupon held that territory.
